newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close firmer on steady Dow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close firmer on steady Dow.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.605 +0.105 Gold NY 368.70 Lon fix 369.00
*Stocks closed at their highs for the session with investors inspired by Friday's stable Dow. Volume 319.0 million, value A$706.5 million, 1,007 stocks traded, 318 steady, 422 up, 267 down
Australian shares finished at their highs for the session on Monday as relieved investors went on the hunt for bargains after the Dow halted its recent sharp pull-back on Friday.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 19.8 points up at 2,336.3, its high for the session.
The December share index ended up 27 points at 2,333 and at a 3.3 point discount to the underlying index.
Investors bid stocks up across the board with cyclical sectors, transport and building materials, amongst the most sought after on the day.
"The big factor today was relief," a Brisbane dealer said.
"The talk on Friday was of an extended fall for the Wall Street market. It didn't happen and now investors are much more confident of the traditional rise to Christmas," he said.
The dealer said fundamental factors like commodity prices had little influence on investors' buying decisions.

"It was all sentiment today - I wouldn't call it a strong bull market but good turnover and the strong debut of Infrastructure Trust (Group of Australia) certainly indicates the return of higher confidence levels," the dealer said.
Although cyclical stocks found the cream of buyers' cash, underpinning the market's rise was solid buying support for the major banks which were hardest hit by selling late last week.
The strong debut of Infrastructure Trust Group of Australia also bolstered sentiment as stags reaped up to a 40 percent premium from the tollway investor's stapled securities.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was lifted by the changing fortunes of Australia's major miners while futures trade was subdued a week closer to the December contract's expiry.
Total options traded 50,464 (45,869)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,553 (13,638).
In other markets, Australian bonds finished firmer on the day where activity was dominated by rollover of expiring December futures contracts.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.32 percent, down 0.09 percentage points from Friday's close.
The Australian dollar killed time in a tight band as investors concentrated on staying out of trouble after a fortnight of wild swings.
At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7927/32.
